name: Public Works
oneLiner: Nonprofit Megaphone as civic infrastructure: a pure-white, flat-block, plain-language site where Google's grant rules are rendered as a public record, the hero object is an exhibit card with a tab, the eligibility check is a real three-box form, and accessibility is the aesthetic.
concept:
Stop designing Nonprofit Megaphone like a marketing agency and design it like the utility it actually is. Nonprofits do not want to be excited about their Ad Grant; they want it to work the way water, transit and the county clerk work: reliably, visibly, under rules everyone can read. Public Works borrows the grammar of public-service design (USWDS, GOV.UK, transit wayfinding, the legal exhibit) and executes it in flat colour on pure white: a civic-blue nav bar, a civic-blue record block, a cool grey band for alternate sections, 2px and 3px rules instead of cards, hard corners, no gradients, no shadows, one typeface, and signal red spent on exactly two things, the button and an 8px square marker. The register is a form you are glad someone filled in for you.

The hero object is the Grant Account Record, drawn as Exhibit A: a white card with a folder-style tab, a 2px ink border, a client-redacted tag, the month, the monthly credit in use as a bordered meter with the $10,000 cap, four numbered Google requirements with blue check squares, and Google's 5% rule restated in plain language in the card's own grey footer. Beneath it, in flow, a named account lead signs one sentence about what they did this month and promises a reply within one business day. On the left the page is a civic form: a numbered section marker, a headline that states the fact in numerals ('$10,000 a month from Google. Kept.'), one sentence of sub copy, the red button with its '15 min' tag, a three-cell ledger of the three real figures, and the eligibility check as three real checkboxes with a 'Check' action, no rep, no form, no JavaScript. The guarantee closes the column as a person: Amber Snow, $25, her email.

It fits Nonprofit Megaphone specifically because every one of its credentials is institutional (Head of Google Ad Grants, one of nine inaugural Certified Professional agencies, a 100% acquisition guarantee, $48M managed, 780+ clients) while the current site renders them in the same SaaS-blue four competitors already occupy. A civic register converts those claims into the visual language of an audit rather than an ad, keeps the mark's #0A23A2 as a working colour rather than a wallpaper, and makes the page forwardable to a board without a rep. The panel's fair criticism was coldness; this version answers it with the human layer above the fold (signed note, Amber's email) and with the exhibit tab and red marker as a signature, not with warmth borrowed from paper.
distinctFrom: The only direction on pure white with flat civic-blue blocks, a single typeface (Public Sans), 2-3px rules and hard corners, whose hero is a tabbed exhibit card and a real checkbox form rather than a diagram, a newspaper, a signed letter or a sticker wall.

palette.note: Pure white page ground, never cream. Documents, forms and the record card are also white; structure is drawn with rules, not surfaces.
Cool light grey for alternate sections (trust band, table headers, the record card's footer). The only alternate ground; a 3px ink rule always opens it.
2px rules for table rows, ledger cells, chip grids and the notice strip. Section boundaries and card borders use ink at 2-3px.
Headlines, body, borders, the Check button and the REDACTED tag. 18.4:1 on white, 16.5:1 on the band (AAA).
Sub copy, labels, captions. 7.7:1 on white, 6.9:1 on the band; safe for 11px uppercase labels.
The mark's blue, used as solid blocks only: nav bar, record block, check squares, meter fill, the word 'Kept.', focus rings, checked-chip text. 11.8:1 with white type.
Meter track and the checked state of eligibility chips. Blue ink on it is 9.9:1.
Small labels and the signed note's byline on the civic-blue block. 7.9:1 on #0A23A2.
Spent on two things only: the primary button (white type 5.3:1) and the 8px square marker that opens every section number, closes the headline and sits on the exhibit tab. Nothing else is red.
The button's hover state only, 160ms colour transition. White type 6.9:1.
Mockup-only: the flat portrait tile behind the account lead's silhouette on the civic-blue block. Replaced by the black-and-white photograph at build; never used as a UI colour.
Mockup-only: the grey silhouette inside portrait placeholders on white (Amber Snow). Decorative, aria-hidden, replaced by photography.

typography.display: Public Sans 800 for h1 and h2, 700 for h3, card titles and the exhibit tab. One family site-wide; the USWDS face is the point.
typography.body: Public Sans 400/500/600. 17px/1.55 on marketing pages (18px hero sub), 16px on the phone, 13.5-14px inside records and tables.
typography.mono: Public Sans (no second family). Every label, unit, date, eyebrow, table header and byline is Public Sans 600, 11-12px, uppercase, 0.08-0.09em tracking, with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on the whole document so figures align without a mono face.
typography.scaleNotes: 8px baseline. h1 62px/1.0/-0.03em/800 on desktop, 40px on the phone, numerals not words ('$10,000'), the final word in civic blue closed by a 14px (11px phone) red square. h2 40px/1.1/-0.03em/800, always preceded by a red square + section number ('02 - The rules'). h3 24px/1.2/700. Body 17px/1.55. Ledger figures 26px/800 with the unit glyph in blue; record figure 38px/800. Labels 11px/600 uppercase, never smaller than 11px and never muted below 6.9:1. Buttons 15-16px/600, 48px tall (52px phone), 2px radius, with an 11px uppercase duration tag behind a 2px white rule. Chips 36px, 13px/500, 2px ink border, 2px radius; checked state flips to blue tint with blue 600 text. Focus ring 3px #0A23A2 offset 2px (white on blue surfaces). Rules: 3px ink for section boundaries, 2px ink for card borders and the eligibility fieldset, 2px #D8DBE0 inside tables. No italics, no shadows, no gradients, nothing above 2px radius.

layout:
GRID AND RHYTHM. 12-column grid, 1200px container, 24px gutters, 40px page margin; spacing scale 8/16/24/40/56/96. Sections are separated by 3px ink rules and, where the ground changes, the #F1F2F4 band; the only solid colour blocks on the page are the civic-blue nav bar, the civic-blue record block, and the ink footer. Every section opens with a red 8px square + number + label eyebrow (sticky at the top of its section) and a left-aligned h2 on columns 1-7, supporting copy or data on columns 8-12. Every figure carries a unit and an as-of date. Print stylesheet ships for case-study records, the rules table and the guarantee page.

- 1. Notice strip (32px, white, 12px, 2px rule beneath): 'Nonprofit Megaphone is one of nine inaugural Google Ad Grants Certified Professional agencies · since 2019'; right, '60+ specialists · Chicago and Beaverton, OR' and the 'Client reports' login link. Leads with the company name so it cannot read as a Google banner.
- 2. Nav bar (64px, civic blue, white type): flat white megaphone mark + wordmark; six links (Ad Grant, Services, Our work, The rules, Pricing, Team) with the active link as a 3px white bottom border inside a full-height flex item; one red 'Book a free call'. One CTA label site-wide. The bar never changes on scroll.
- 3. Hero (cols 1-7 / 8-12, 26px top padding): eyebrow '01 - Google Ad Grant management'; h1 '$10,000 a month from Google. Kept.' with 'Kept.' in blue and the red end-mark; one-sentence 18px sub; red button with '15 min' tag + underlined 'See a real account report' (opens a redacted PDF); a three-cell ledger (780+ nonprofits managed · as of Sep 2026 / $48M+ ad spend managed · cumulative / 100% grant acquisition · guaranteed) with tabular figures and blue unit glyphs; the eligibility fieldset under a 2px rule: 'Am I eligible? Three checks · 2 min · no rep, no form' with three real checkboxes drawn as chips (501(c)(3) / Not a hospital, school or government / Has a website) and an ink 'Check' action; the guarantee line with a flat portrait: 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy. Unhappy at any point? Meet our CEO, Amber Snow, and we'll give you $25. Email Amber directly.' Right column: the civic-blue record block (18px padding, flex column, 14px gap) holding Exhibit A (tab, 'Form NPM-01 · Sample record' label, header with title / CLIENT REDACTED / Aug 2026, monthly credit in use $8,940 of $10,000 with a bordered meter and '89.4% used · NPM client median, 12 mo · cap $10,000', four numbered requirements with blue check squares and the 5% floor in ink 700, and the plain-language footer on the grey band) and, in flow beneath it, the signed one-sentence note from the named account lead with portrait and 'Replies within 1 business day'.
- 4. Trust band (#F1F2F4, 3px ink rule above): cols 1-4, '02 - Endorsement · Google' with the Michelle Hurtado quote and her title; cols 5-12, 'Trusted by 780+ nonprofits · as of Sep 2026' over a 4x2 client table drawn with 2px #D8DBE0 rules and white cells: UNCF, Scouting America, COPD Foundation, YWCA Chicago, Earthwatch, AAU, Solar Sister, JFCS in four alternating Public Sans treatments; monochrome vector logos at a fixed cap height replace them once licensed.
- 5. '03 - This month, in one sentence': the retreat candid runs full-width inside a 2px ink frame with, on cols 8-12, a CMS-driven card: one real dated sentence from a named account lead about a real (redacted) account, signed. The human artefact within the first two scrolls.
- 6. '04 - The rules': a six-row table, Requirement / What Google does if you miss it / What we do about it (5% CTR floor, conversion tracking, two sitelinks, geo-targeting, Smart bidding, annual survey), each middle cell citing Google's policy page with the date checked; printable to one page.
- 7. '05 - Proof': case studies as records: a filterable table, Organization / Cause / CTR / Conversion rate / Outcome per month / Period / Named contact + title, with a 'Forward to board' PDF action per row; six rows on home, link to all 54, filterable by the 12 verticals. Every case-study page opens with the same fixed three-figure header; screenshots carry a visible REDACTED tag, never a blur.
- 8. '06 - Services': a numbered index 01-07 (Ad Grant Management, Website SEO, Content Creation, VisitorEmail, Google Remarketing, Microsoft Advertising, Spanish Ad Creation), each one row: number, name, one plain sentence, price range or 'included', arrow. No icons.
- 9. '07 - Pricing and how it works': flat monthly fee stated as a range (the client supplies the number; the slot will not ship as 'contact us'), 'no % of spend' as a label, the six-step process, and the eligibility checker in full: four questions, one check square filling per answer, ending in the booking form or an honest 'You're not eligible, here's why' card for hospitals, schools and governments with the two alternatives NPM can still offer.
- 10. '08 - Your account team': the real 60 as a directory: eye-level black-and-white portraits at 4:5 with a 2px ink border and a 'Nonprofits I support' caption, name, role; sortable by vertical. Amber Snow and Grant Hensel appear in the same grid at the same size.
- 11. Guarantee block (band, 3px ink rules, ink type with the promise in blue): 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy.' then 'Unhappy? Meet our CEO, Amber Snow, and we'll give you $25.' with her plain-text email and the terms set as a small ruled plate. Red stays unique to the button and the marker; the block is not red.
- 12. Final CTA: one line, one red button with the '15 min' tag, the HubSpot form inline with 48px fields, 2px ink borders and blue focus rings, fine print 'Flat monthly fee · no % of spend · no contract to talk'.
- 13. Footer (ink, white type): four columns of links, address, phone, socials as text, Google Partner and Certified Professional badges on a white tile so their own blue has a compliant home, newsletter, Terms of Use, and the figure ledger repeated with its as-of date.

INTERIOR PAGES inherit the sticky numbered markers, open with one photograph above the fold inside a 2px ink frame, and use the same three-figure header. A locked style-guide page documents the class set for Webflow editors: spacing tokens, the three block colours, one type family, the 2/3px rule system, the exhibit tab, the red marker, and the rule that every figure carries unit + date.
imagery: No illustration system, no icons beyond the check square and the arrow, no stock. Four image classes. (1) Documents: the Grant Account Record, the reporting dashboard, the rules table and case-study records are typeset in HTML as white cards with 2px ink borders, a folder tab where the object is an exhibit, tabular figures and uppercase labels; these are the hero images of the site. Real screenshots inside them carry a visible REDACTED tag on an ink field rather than a blur. (2) People: the 60 staff re-shot or re-processed to one standard: eye-level, natural light, black-and-white, 4:5, 2px ink border, caption 'Nonprofits I support'; account leads appear at 44x55 beside their signed note (white border on the blue block) and at full size in the directory; the wood-panelled retreat candid runs full-width, unretouched, in section 03. The mockups use flat grey silhouettes as placeholders and say so. (3) Client evidence: consented photography from client nonprofits shown only inside case-study records, cropped to the grid, captioned with org, program and year; no reaching hands, no globes, no heart-in-hands. (4) Form furniture: the red 8px square marker, the numbered field labels (01-04), the check square, the bordered meter with its cap mark, and the exhibit tab; these recur on every page and are the only decoration. Charts follow one rule set: bar and line only, civic-blue fill on blue-tint track, 2px #D8DBE0 gridlines, every axis labelled with units and an as-of date, a sourced footnote under every chart, and the 5% CTR floor drawn as a 2px ink dashed line on every CTR chart. The megaphone mark is redrawn as flat vector; it is white on the blue bar and blue on white, never two-tone.
motion: Motion is functional and short, like a well-made transit sign. Global: 160ms ease-out for hover and focus; every animation is wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference so the reduced-motion default is the static state. Buttons: on hover red deepens to #B01F15 and the arrow translates 4px; on focus the 3px ring appears instantly. Eligibility chips: :checked flips the chip to blue tint and fills the check square, CSS-only, no transition needed. The record meter fills from 0 to its value once on load over 900ms with cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); this is the one choreographed moment and it is already in the mockup. Tables: rows reveal with a 40ms stagger using animation-timeline: view() where supported; static rendering elsewhere, stated. Row hover fills with blue tint. Section markers pin to the top of their section (position: sticky). Nav: no transparency, no blur, never changes on scroll. Nothing parallaxes, nothing floats, no smooth-scroll library, no Lottie. Interaction JS under 4kB (the checker's result card and the table filters); everything else is CSS.
mobile: The 390px hero is a civic form, not the desktop squeezed. Nav is a 56px blue bar: white mark + wordmark, a 36px red 'Book a call' button (the only place the CTA label shortens, for width) and a 40px menu button. Hero: red square + '01 - Google Ad Grant management'; h1 at 40px/1.0 set as three deliberate lines, '$10,000 a month / from Google. / Kept.' with the red mark after 'Kept.'; one 16px sentence; then the eligibility fieldset under a 3px ink rule as a real form: 'Am I eligible?' with three 48px rows, each a numbered label (01-03) with a 22px checkbox, 2px rules between, and 'Three ticks = eligible · Check my answers' beneath; then the full-width 52px red button 'Book a free call · 15 min' and the underlined 'See a real account report'. The button's bottom edge sits at about 616px from the top, so headline, the three checks, the CTA and the eligibility link are all inside the first 700px. A three-cell ledger (780+ / $48M+ / 100%) closes the hero. Below the fold the civic-blue block carries Exhibit A at full width (tab, header, meter, four requirement rows, plain-language footer) with the signed note in flow beneath it, then the grey trust band with the Michelle Hurtado endorsement and the Amber Snow guarantee. Key sections: tables become stacked records with the same three-figure header; the rules table becomes six numbered cards; the client table becomes a 2x4 grid; the team directory becomes two columns of 4:5 portraits; the sticky section marker persists at 12px. Tap targets are 48px minimum throughout.
a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor and most pairs clear AAA: ink on white 18.4:1, ink on band 16.5:1, muted #4E5360 on white 7.7:1 and on band 6.9:1, white on civic blue 11.8:1, on-blue label #C9D2F7 7.9:1, white on signal red 5.3:1 (button type is 15-16px/600), red on white 5.3:1, blue on tint 9.9:1. Smallest text anywhere is 11px, and only for uppercase 600-weight labels at 6.9:1 or better. Body 16-18px. Focus: a visible 3px #0A23A2 outline offset 2px on every link, button and checkbox label (white on blue surfaces), never removed. The eligibility chips are real <input type=checkbox> elements with <label for>, inside a <fieldset> with a <legend>, so they work with keyboard and screen readers without JavaScript. Exhibit A is a <figure> with an aria-label that states every figure in prose (credit in use, median, the four requirements and their thresholds), the meter and the check squares are aria-hidden, the requirement list has an accessible name, and the footer is the figcaption. The red square markers, portrait placeholders, the mark and every decorative SVG are aria-hidden; the arrow glyphs are aria-hidden with the link text carrying the meaning. Colour is never the only carrier: checked chips gain a check glyph and weight, the 5% floor is labelled in words, the active nav link is bold as well as underlined. Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion (all animation sits inside a no-preference media query). Landmarks: nav with aria-label, sections labelled by heading or aria-label, aria-current on the active link. 48px targets on desktop buttons, 48-52px on the phone. Print stylesheet for records and the rules table.

heroCopy.headline: $10,000 a month from Google. Kept.
heroCopy.sub: We acquire the Google Ad Grant, keep it inside Google's rules every month, and put it to work for your mission.

signatureMoments: Exhibit A: the Grant Account Record as a white card with a folder tab and a 2px ink border on a flat civic-blue block; CLIENT REDACTED and the month in the header, $8,940 of $10,000 on a bordered meter with the cap marked, four numbered Google requirements with blue check squares, and Google's 5% rule restated in plain language in the card's own grey footer, then a named account lead signing one sentence beneath it.

The eligibility check as a real form in the hero: three checkboxes drawn as chips (501(c)(3) / Not a hospital, school or government / Has a website) that flip to blue tint when ticked, with an ink 'Check' action; the rep-free path visible without a click and working without JavaScript. On the phone it becomes three 48px numbered rows under 'Am I eligible?'.

'Kept.' as the whole promise: a 62px Public Sans 800 headline stated in numerals that ends in one blue word closed by a red square, the same 8px square that opens every section number and sits on every exhibit tab.

The ledger row: 780+ / $48M+ / 100% as three ruled cells with tabular figures, blue unit glyphs and a dated qualifier on a second line, so the three facts read as an audited table rather than bold words in a paragraph.

'04 - The rules': the Requirement / What Google does if you miss it / What we do about it table with the policy page cited and dated in every row, making NPM the only agency site that teaches the policy before selling against it; printable to one page for a board.
dependencies: Consent for a real record: Exhibit A's figures ($8,940 / 89.4% / 7.9% CTR / 4 sitelinks) are illustrative placeholders. The build needs one real anonymised client account with written permission plus a real trailing-12-month client median from NPM's reporting, shown as it is even if lower.

Name the account leads: the signed one-sentence monthly note requires a named lead per account, a portrait, and an operations commitment to write it monthly ('Maya R.' in the mockup is a placeholder).
Publish pricing: 'Pricing' in the nav and the flat-fee range in section 07 need a leadership decision; the design reserves the slot and will not ship 'contact us' in it.
Publish the rules: 'The rules' commits the client to citing Google's policy pages with dates checked and to keeping them current (a quarterly review).
Photography: 60 portraits re-shot or re-processed to one black-and-white 4:5 standard, and the retreat candid cleared for use.
Amber Snow's real email under the guarantee and a real 'Client reports' login and 'See a real account report' PDF at launch, or those links are removed.
Client logo licences for the eight wordmarks, so the typographic client table can swap to monochrome vector logos.
A locked Webflow class set and style-guide page as a costed deliverable so the no-radius, no-shadow, two-block-colour discipline survives handover.
risks: Institutional register can still read cold if the client cuts the human layer. The direction depends on four real artefacts: a named lead's monthly sentence, Amber Snow's email, the retreat candid at section 03, and re-shot portraits. Without them the flat blocks and form grammar tip toward a government portal.

Illustrative record figures are a liability on a page whose whole argument is sourcing; if a real permitted account cannot be obtained, the card must be labelled 'Illustrative' in the header, and implying full $10k spend must be avoided (the audience reads that as an overpromise).

Pure white, hard corners and one grotesk sit one notch from a dev-tool template. The exhibit tab, the red marker, the ledger and the portraits are the counterweights; if the Webflow build drops the 2/3px rule system or adds radius and shadow, the page falls back toward generic.

Public Sans single-family is deliberately plain and can look less 'designed' next to a serif-led direction in the pitch room; the craft is in the spacing, the rules and the record. Mixing in a second family is not permitted.

The CTA colour moves from coral #DA6343 to signal red #D0261B and brand blue moves from page ground to a 64px bar and a contained block; position this to 780 existing clients and Google's partner directory as sharpening, and confirm the mark's actual blue before promising continuity.
The phone nav shortens the CTA to 'Book a call' for width; if one label site-wide is non-negotiable, drop the wordmark to the mark alone on phones.
Google Partner and Certified Professional badge usage rules (clear space, permitted backgrounds) must be checked for the white footer tile; the badges must not sit on the blue block or beside red.
animation-timeline: view() lacks Safari and Firefox support; table reveals render static there, and that is acceptable and stated.
references: USWDS (designsystem.digital.gov): Public Sans, the banner pattern, focus states as design, flat semantic colour tokens
GOV.UK Design System: plain-language headlines, thick black rules, one-question-per-page checker logic, the checkbox component
Legal exhibit tabs and IRS/Form 990 typesetting: the record card's tab, numbered fields and cap marks
NYC MTA / TfL wayfinding: flat blocks, numbered routes, high-contrast type, end-marks
Mercury.com: tabular numerals, one action colour, financial documents as UI
Stripe and Ramp annual updates: proof rendered as ledgers with dates and sources
Swiss International style (Muller-Brockmann): the grid, the single accent, the discipline of one family
Vercel.com: uppercase labels and black-and-white discipline, deliberately without the dark ground or the dev-tool coldness
